name: Diotrephes
overview: Diotrephes is a male figure noted in the New Testament for his desire to be first in the church, yet he refuses to accept the teachings and authority of the Apostle John. His conduct illustrates a problematic leadership within the early Christian community, marked by a rejection of apostolic instruction.
namesAndTitles: The name Diotrephes appears as a proper name in Scripture without any specific meaning provided in the text. There are no additional titles or meanings associated with his name in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Diotrephes beyond what is indicated by his actions and role within the church community.
scriptureSignificance: Diotrephes is significant in the biblical narrative as an example of a church leader who seeks preeminence for himself rather than submission to apostolic authority. His refusal to accept John's message highlights the challenges faced by the early church in maintaining doctrinal unity and humility among its leaders. This situation serves as a warning against pride and divisiveness within Christian fellowship.
